title: Hybrid-stripe KV coalescing for cross-parallel memory compaction
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: As we scale inference for long-context workloads across heterogeneous multi-GPU topologies, per-GPU KV slab fragmentation and cross-parallel placement mismatches increase memory pressure and force early KV spills. This ticket proposes a hybrid-stripe KV coalescing mechanism that dynamically compacts and rebalances KV segments across tensor- and pipeline-parallel boundaries to reduce total device memory usage and improve continuous batching efficiency.

Goals:
- Reduce peak GPU memory used for KV cache by 15-30% on mixed tensor/pipeline topologies.
- Minimize added latency during online coalescing (target < 2 ms tail per request).
- Preserve correctness of KV lookups across pipeline stages and avoid extra cross-device synchronous hops on the critical path.
- Integrate with current continuous batching and KV prefetch policies to avoid regression on short/interactive requests.

Proposed approach:
1) Hybrid-stripe layout: keep logical KV segments partitioned into variable-sized "stripes" whose width is chosen by a placement estimator based on per-device free memory, expected sequence-length distribution, and model kv-sparsity. Stripes can be pinned to a single device or mirrored across devices if hot.
2) Opportunistic coalescer: background compaction task that merges small/adjacent stripes into larger contiguous allocations on the most memory-rich device(s) using an asynchronous copy + pointer-redirect approach. Coalescing is throttled by an adaptive budget tied to CPU/GPU utilization and current latency SLO headroom.
3) Cross-parallel mapping layer: introduce a lightweight indirection table that maps logical stripe IDs to physical device locations and offsets. The lookup is kept in CPU memory and cached per worker; a fast-path exists for majority cases with local stripe placement to avoid cross-device RPCs.
4) Pipeline-aware handoff: when pipeline-parallel stages require a remote stripe, pre-scheduled prefetch hooks are used (leveraging existing KV prefetch infra) to warm local copies or temporary shared pinned buffers so the forward pass avoids on-critical-path transfers.
5) Integration with continuous batching: the batching coordinator is extended to include stripe placement hints so that request coalescing prefers requests with colocated hot stripes to maximize cache locality.

Trade-offs considered:
- Eager mirroring of hot stripes reduces remote access but increases total memory usage; we select mirroring only when metrics show net latency benefit under expected QPS.
- Moving stripes can cause transient double-memory usage during copy; we bound concurrent moves and prefer low-traffic windows.
- Indirection table introduces CPU-side metadata overhead; we keep entries compact and evict rarely-used entries from worker caches.

Acceptance criteria and telemetry:
- Benchmarks show >=15% reduction in peak KV memory on a heterogeneous 4-GPU (A100+T4 mix) testbed for long-context evals (8k tokens) with baseline continuous batching.
- P50/P95 latency for chat-style 256-token interactive QPS remains within 5% of baseline.
- No increase in error rates or incorrect KV retrievals.
- New metrics: stripe_move_rate, stripe_mirroring_ratio, stripe_local_hit_rate, coalescer_cpu_budget_utilization. Dashboards linked in attachments.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1: Local simulation and microbenchmarks (unit tests for correctness of mapping and copy).
- Stage 2: Canary on Dedicated cluster with synthetic long-context workload; enable coalescer in read-only mode (moves simulated) to validate metrics.
- Stage 3: Gradual enable with low-percentage traffic, automatic rollback if stripe_move_rate or latency regressions exceed thresholds.

Compatibility notes:
- Backwards compatible with existing KV slab formats; we will add a migration tool to rebuild stripe metadata for pinned deployments.
- Private deployments will be able to opt-in; default is disabled for on-prem to avoid surprise memory behavior.

comments: 2025-01-13 - Aisha Khan: Kickoff meeting notes added. Agreed to keep initial coalescer single-threaded and conservative budget; Diego to prototype copy+pointer-redirect API.

2025-01-20 - Diego Martin: Prototype implements stripe indirection table and simulated coalesce. Initial microbench shows 18% reduction in peak KV memory on homogeneous 8-GPU A100 cluster, but heterogeneous tests pending.
2025-01-22 - Claire Wu (review): Reviewed mapping API. Concern: CPU lookup cache could be hot on high QPS. Suggested adding per-worker LRU and stats tags. Action: Diego to add LRU and histograms.

2025-01-28 - Diego Martin: Added per-worker LRU and histograms. Benchmarks on mixed A100+T4 setup show 13% peak reduction; discrepancy due to copy throttling. Tuning budget increased improvement to 17% at cost of 0.8 ms extra background CPU time.

2025-01-30 - Ben Torres (perf): Ran stress tests with continuous batching enabled. Observed small P95 latency tail when coalescer ran concurrently with large batch drains. Mitigation: coalescer will check batching coordinator headroom before starting heavy copies.

2025-02-02 - Elena Petrova (security): Quick review on indirection metadata. No secrets handled. Recommended adding bounds checks on pointer redirection to avoid out-of-bounds copies. Diego to add asserts and sanitizers.

2025-02-04 - Diego Martin: Implemented safety checks and canary config flags. Preparing PR for internal review. Next steps: add canary run on dedicated-qa and collect stripe_local_hit_rate and stripe_move_rate over 72h.
2025-02-04 - Aisha Khan: Moving ticket to In Progress. PM to coordinate canary schedule with SRE.
